Intraoperative dosing and lactate appear both in the text (1.5-h procedure) and in Table 5 (Intraoperative core period 0.5 h). The table row covers a 0.5 h core period, so text dosing facts and table facts were kept separate instead of merged. Central venous pressure units differ: the intraoperative change is printed in mmHg ("from 25 to 18 mmHg") while the monitoring target and the limitations paragraph print CVP in cmH2O (10–15). The measured values are kept with the printed unit and not converted.

Table cross-references in the text look mismatched: the LVEF stratification is Table 1 although the text cites Table 2 for it, and the Discussion cites Table 3 for the stratification framework. The article-wide table numbering is not relied on.

The limitations paragraph states the dose of dobutamine was limited due to the presence of left ventricular thrombus. This is recorded as a dobutamine fact (p1-f207) without a dose or time; it is not attached to any specific dobutamine dose.

Table 6 timeline rows summarize events narratively (for example Day 1 antibiotics initiated and CRRT, Day 3 emergency debridement); discrete values were captured as facts only where the row gives a value or a labelled time. The text times antibiotics as intraoperative and CRRT without a time.

Two debridements are described (initial urgent surgical debridement and the March 8 further debridement). The clinical-findings sentence "Skin necrosis, subcutaneous crepitus, and right great saphenous vein thrombosis were noted upon surgical debridement" does not say which; these findings are not linked to either debridement event.

The clinical-findings paragraph says "Postoperatively, the patient was transferred to the ICU with persistent tachycardia" without naming the operation; the text also places the patient in the ICU before the March 8 surgery ("After initial resuscitation in the ICU ... on the morning of surgery"). The tachycardia fact is not linked to the post-March-8 ICU transfer event.

Table 6 Day 3 (Intraoperative) says lactate normalized to 1.7 mmol/L; Table 5 prints 1.7 for both the intraoperative core period and the end of surgery, and the text gives 1.7 at the end of surgery. The Table 6 value is kept as its own fact because the source does not say which measurement it is.

The Day 5 TTE (LVEF 22%, thrombus stable) is printed in Table 5 as "Repeat TTE at Day 5" within the ICU Days 2–5 row and in Table 6 as "TTE on Day 5" within the Postoperative Days 1–5 row. Both print the same Day 5 label and identical findings and are kept as one study; the implied day-count anchors (ICU day versus postoperative day) differ.

The Table 2 (Baseline patient characteristics) laboratory row has no time label of its own; Pro-BNP 12,140.5 pg/mL is also given by the text as an initial laboratory test and lactate 4.6 mmol/L as the admission value, so those two are each one item citing text and table. CRP 214.0 mg/L and elevated troponin T are kept from Table 2 without a time.
